questions.question: How did the Prime Minister debate about the delaying of the government's response towards Covid-19?
questions.reference_answer: In response to the opposition party, the Prime Minister answered that the government rolled out the Canada emergency response benefit extremely quickly, and they had been helping the small businesses with the Canada emergency business account. The opposition party was not very satisfied because he thought that the government did not reach out to as many businesses as possible. Also, the opposition party made a few comments on the rent relief program which was too rigid and hard to apply.

oracle.answer: The Prime Minister, Justin Trudeau, did not directly address a debate about delaying the government's response towards Covid-19. Instead, he emphasized the swift action taken by the government, such as rolling out the Canada Emergency Response Benefit and wage subsidies. He acknowledged that certain businesses face difficulties qualifying for aid but stated that the government is working to fill these gaps and assist businesses through regional development agencies. Trudeau defended the government’s efforts, indicating ongoing work to support businesses and workers affected by the pandemic.

questions.question: What did the opposition party and the Prime Minister commented about companies laying off workers in the midst of pandemic?
questions.reference_answer: The Prime Minister explained that the government recognized that several organizations and companies were facing difficulties because of COVID-19 and they were supporting people all over the country through that program. Although the opposition party was getting rigorous about the intensity of the question, the Prime Minister kept emphasizing that the government's priority had always been workers in difficulty so that they do not lose their jobs. This applied to all organizations and companies in the country to the extent possible.

oracle.answer:
The opposition party, represented by Mr. Yves-François Blanchet, questioned whether the Liberal Party of Canada was taking advantage of emergency programs meant for companies and organizations facing difficulties due to the pandemic. He repeatedly asked if the Liberal Party itself was in difficulty and suggested that the criteria for determining organizational difficulty might be poorly designed if the Liberal Party could qualify.

The Prime Minister, Justin Trudeau, did not directly address whether the Liberal Party was in difficulty. Instead, he emphasized that the government's focus was on supporting workers and organizations facing difficulties due to COVID-19. He stated that the criteria for the programs were designed to help those in need and that the government was committed to assisting workers and companies across the country.

questions.question: What was the debate over the situation of long-term care?
questions.reference_answer: The opposition party questioned about sending military groups to provinces in order to fix long-term care. The Prime Minister answered that the government needed to make sure seniors across the country were properly cared for, and they sent in the military to help the provinces. The opposition party also questioned about applying the national standards so that long-term care was governed by the same principles as the Canada Health Act. The Prime Minister elaborated that due the Covid-19, pushing the project had become extremely difficult.

oracle.answer: The debate over the situation of long-term care involved Mr. Jagmeet Singh pressing the Prime Minister to take federal leadership and action on improving long-term care conditions, which he argued were appalling based on military reports. Singh called for an end to profit in long-term care and the establishment of national standards similar to the Canada Health Act. The Prime Minister, Justin Trudeau, acknowledged the seriousness of the situation and the need for improvement but emphasized that the federal government respects provincial jurisdiction over long-term care facilities. Trudeau stated that the federal government is committed to working with the provinces to address these issues and ensure proper support for seniors across the country.

He also asked whether the infection of 39 Canadian Armed Forces members with COVID-19 could have been due to improper protocols in the facilities. The Minister explained that community outreach was a very important part of the work of a member of Parliament and WeChat was one of many social media sites regularly used by members, and the minister did not share any personal views on Wechat.

questions.question: What was the debate about the economic bilateral relations with the UK?
questions.reference_answer: The opposition party claimed that the government was not cooperating with the UK, its largest trading partner, protecting the viability of their international supply chains and capitalizing on the opportunities. The minister explained that the UK, of course, was a very important trading partner for Canada, and CETA would continue to apply to trade with the U.K. during this period while they went through Brexit.

Mr. Hoback questioned whether the government would commit to having a new trade agreement with the UK in place by January 1 to avoid these tariffs. Minister Mary Ng assured that the situation was being monitored closely and that CETA continues to apply to trade with the UK during the Brexit transition period. There was no explicit mention of a new trade agreement being finalized by the specified date.

questions.question: What was the discussion about imports and supply chains?
questions.reference_answer: The opposition party claimed that the supply chain in Canada amidst the pandemic was not stable enough and the government was not doing anything. The minister explained that they would continue to work with countries around the globe to ensure that Canada's supply chains and those global supply chains, particularly for essential goods, for agricultural products, for medical supplies, would continue to remain open.

There was also mention of ongoing efforts to resolve issues like the status of canola exports to China.

questions.question: What was the controversy about China hoarding PPE amid the pandemic?
questions.reference_answer: The opposition party claimed that China was procuring and hoarding PPE during January. And in April, the minister stated there were not enough supplies in the national emergency stockpile. The opposition party was triggered by the fact that the minister approved a donation of 16 tonnes of PPE for China on January 31, claiming it would not compromise the country's supply. The minister explained that the government was doing so because they had multiple complementary supply chains operating at the same time for PPE production.

oracle.answer: The controversy about China hoarding PPE amid the pandemic involves reports that senior Canadian bureaucrats received credible information in early January indicating China was procuring and hoarding personal protective equipment (PPE). Despite these reports, the health minister approved a donation of 16 tonnes of PPE to China on January 31, stating it would not compromise Canada's supply. This decision is questioned given later statements by the minister acknowledging shortages in the national emergency stockpile. The health minister defended the donation by explaining it consisted of nearly expired or expired goods that China needed during its outbreak. However, opposition members like Mrs. Cathy McLeod argue that these supplies could have been more effectively used by Canadian hospitals and care homes during February and March.

The opposition party pointed out that these failures were the product of systemic neglect.The minister replied that they were fully aware that in long-term care facilities both seniors and persons living with a disability face unique challenges. And considering the severity of this report, the federal government promptly shared it with the Province of Ontario, and the Province of Ontario has initiated an investigation based on the report's findings.
